comments.content: The `chassert(started_file->getFileStatus()->processed_rows > 0)` here is risky. When `isCancelled()` is true but the reader was just created and no chunk has been pulled yet (processed_rows == 0), this assertion will fire in debug builds. The original code handled this case by only calling `setFailed` when `file_status->processed_rows` was non-zero. Consider guarding the assertion or handling the zero-rows case explicitly.

Same concern as above for the `table_is_being_dropped` branch: `chassert(started_file->getFileStatus()->processed_rows > 0)` may fire if the file was just started and no rows were read yet. The previous implementation checked `file_status->processed_rows == 0` and simply broke out of the loop in that case.

When an error occurs during read, the code now returns `{}` unconditionally without calling `file_iterator->returnForRetry(...)`. Previously, if `processed_rows == 0` and retries were below max, the file was returned for retry. With the new flow, the retry is presumably handled via `setFailed(..., reduce_retry_count=true)` in `commit`, but the file iterator's in-memory retry queue is no longer updated. Verify that the retry mechanism still works correctly for files that failed before any rows were read.

`resetProcessing()` now throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` if `processing_id_version` is not set. However, `setFailed()` calls `resetProcessing()` in the `else` branch (when `reduce_retry_count` is false). If `setFailed` is invoked on a file whose state is `Failed` (not `Processing`), `resetProcessing` will throw because the state check at the top of `resetProcessing` requires `Processing`. Confirm that `setFailed` is never called on a file that is not in `Processing` state, or add a state guard before calling `resetProcessing`.

The `file_status->onFailed(exception_message)` call was moved to after the `resetProcessing()` call. If `resetProcessing()` throws (e.g., due to a Keeper error), `onFailed` will never be invoked, leaving the file status inconsistent. Consider whether `onFailed` should be called before the ZK operations, or wrap the reset in a try/catch.

In the MULTI_READ branch, when `responses[0]->error == ZOK` but `get_response->data.empty()`, `processed_node` remains `std::nullopt` and `processed_node_stat` is left default-initialized. Later, `if (processed_node.has_value())` will be false, so `addCheckNotExistsRequest` is used. This matches the non-MULTI_READ path behavior, but note that the non-MULTI_READ path also checks `failed_node_path` existence only when `getMaxProcessedFile` returns true. The MULTI_READ path checks `failed_node_path` unconditionally, which is a behavior change — verify this is intentional.

Removing the `makeCheckRequest(processing_node_id_path, processing_id_version.value())` before `makeRemoveRequest` changes the semantics: previously the multi-op would fail atomically if the version didn't match; now the remove itself carries the version, which is equivalent. This is fine, but ensure all callers relying on the check-then-remove pattern are updated consistently (the unordered variant was also changed).

`setProcessedImpl(bool remove_processing_nodes_only)` is still declared but the `resetProcessingImpl` override was removed. Since `resetProcessingImpl` is no longer virtual in the base class, this declaration is now dead code. Consider removing it to avoid confusion.

The test now calls `node.query("system stop merges")` but never restores merges if the test fails before `system start merges`. Consider using a try/finally to ensure merges are restarted, otherwise subsequent tests in the same node may be affected.
